newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel cancels daily monetary tender.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel cancels daily monetary tender.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Thursday it cancelled its daily monetary tender to commercial banks because of excess liquidity.
The central bank did not say when it would renew the tenders.
In the past few months the central bank has periodically suspended the tenders, which provide liquidity to the banking system.
Much of the excess liquidity has been due to dollar buying by the central bank to prevent the shekel from appreciating too strongly against the official currency basket to which it is pegged.
The central bank has also blamed loose fiscal policy for the excess liquidity.
The daily tenders were previously cancelled on October 2 and did not resume until October 16.
In July the central bank's weekly tenders were halted and have yet to be resumed.
